protocols.name: Three-phase motor power
protocols.security: Not a data link; hazardous voltage, isolate and lock out before work
protocols.description: Three-phase AC (often PWM inverter output) feeding induction, PMSM and BLDC motors.

protocols.name: DC power
protocols.security: Not a data link
protocols.description: DC supply rails (e.g. 5 V, 12 V, 24 V, 48 V) distributing power to robot subsystems.

protocols.name: PWM signal
protocols.typical_rate: 50 Hz (RC servo) to tens of kHz
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring
protocols.description: Pulse-width modulated logic signal: RC servo/ESC command (1-2 ms pulses at 50-400 Hz) or power-stage gate/LED dimming.

protocols.name: Analog 0-10 V
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring
protocols.description: Voltage analog signal common for sensors, VFD speed references and building automation; sensitive to ground offsets.

protocols.name: Analog 4-20 mA current loop
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring
protocols.description: Current loop for process sensors and actuators; live zero (4 mA) allows wire-break detection (< 3.6 mA per NAMUR NE 43).

protocols.name: Discrete digital I/O
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring
protocols.description: 24 V PLC-style or logic-level discrete inputs/outputs (PNP/NPN, sourcing/sinking) for switches, interlocks and solenoids.

protocols.name: Step/direction
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring
protocols.description: Pulse-train position command (one pulse per microstep plus direction line) for stepper and servo drives.

protocols.name: Incremental quadrature (A/B/Z)
protocols.typical_rate: up to several MHz edge rate
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring
protocols.description: Two 90-degree phase-shifted channels plus optional index from incremental encoders; TTL or RS-422 differential line drivers.

protocols.name: Synchronous Serial Interface (SSI)
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring
protocols.description: Clocked RS-422 serial interface for absolute encoder position; no standardized command channel.

protocols.name: BiSS C
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring; CRC protects integrity only
protocols.description: Open bidirectional serial encoder protocol (iC-Haus) with CRC, register access and line-delay compensation.

protocols.name: EnDat 2.2
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring; CRC protects integrity only
protocols.description: HEIDENHAIN bidirectional digital encoder interface with position, diagnostics and additional data; functional-safety variants exist.

protocols.name: HIPERFACE DSL
protocols.topology: point-to-point, single cable with motor power
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring; CRC protects integrity only
protocols.description: SICK digital motor-feedback protocol on two wires integrated into the motor power cable; SIL-capable variants.

protocols.name: Resolver excitation/feedback
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring
protocols.description: Analog sine/cosine rotary transformer feedback; robust to heat and vibration, decoded by an RDC.

protocols.name: I2C
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring
protocols.description: Two-wire on-board bus (SDA/SCL, open drain) for sensors, EEPROMs and PMICs.

protocols.name: SPI
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring
protocols.description: De facto 4-wire synchronous serial bus for ADCs, IMUs, flash and displays.

protocols.name: UART (TTL serial)
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring; debug consoles are a common attack surface
protocols.description: Asynchronous serial at logic levels; GPS modules, debug consoles, smart servos.

protocols.name: RS-232
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring
protocols.description: Single-ended serial line (+/-3 to 15 V) for legacy instruments and service ports; ~15 m cable.

protocols.name: RS-485
protocols.typical_rate: up to 10 Mbit/s (short), 100 kbit/s at 1200 m
protocols.topology: multi-drop differential bus, 120 Ohm terminated at both ends
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring
protocols.description: Differential multi-drop physical layer under Modbus RTU, PROFIBUS DP, DMX and many smart servo buses.

protocols.name: USB
protocols.security: No device authentication in common use; malicious devices (HID injection) are a known risk
protocols.description: Host-device bus for cameras, adapters, storage and debug; USB-C also carries USB PD power.

protocols.name: 1-Wire
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring; some devices offer SHA-256 authentication
protocols.description: Single data-line bus (Maxim/ADI) for temperature sensors, ID chips and battery authentication.

protocols.name: MIPI I3C
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring
protocols.description: Successor to I2C with in-band interrupts, dynamic addressing and higher speed; backward compatible with many I2C devices.

protocols.name: MIPI CSI-2
protocols.security: No link-layer authentication by default
protocols.description: Camera serial interface over D-PHY/C-PHY lanes from image sensor to ISP; short PCB/flex distances.

protocols.name: GMSL (Gigabit Multimedia Serial Link)
protocols.topology: point-to-point serializer/deserializer over coax or STP
protocols.security: No authentication; physical security
protocols.description: Analog Devices SerDes extending camera/display links over up to ~15 m coax, carrying power and control backchannel.

protocols.name: PCI Express
protocols.security: Devices have DMA access; use an IOMMU; IDE/TDISP add link encryption in newer revisions
protocols.description: High-speed expansion bus for accelerators, NVMe, NICs and frame grabbers.

protocols.name: LIN
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring
protocols.description: Low-cost single-wire automotive sub-bus for body electronics, small actuators and sensors.

protocols.name: FlexRay
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring
protocols.description: Deterministic time-triggered automotive bus for chassis and x-by-wire systems.

protocols.name: Quad SPI (QSPI/OSPI)
protocols.typical_rate: up to ~133 MHz x 4 data lines
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring; external flash contents can be read or altered unless encrypted/authenticated by the MCU
protocols.description: Multi-line SPI variant for execute-in-place NOR flash and PSRAM on MCUs and FPGAs.

protocols.name: SD/SDIO
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring
protocols.description: SD card storage interface and SDIO peripherals such as Wi-Fi/BT modules on embedded boards.

protocols.name: HDMI
protocols.security: HDCP content protection only; DDC/CEC side channels are unauthenticated
protocols.description: Digital video/audio output to monitors and HMI panels; also input on capture devices.

protocols.name: DisplayPort
protocols.security: HDCP content protection only
protocols.description: VESA digital display interface, also carried over USB-C alt mode; eDP variant for embedded panels.

protocols.name: CAN 2.0 (Classical CAN)
protocols.topology: multi-drop bus, 120 Ohm termination at both ends
protocols.security: No authentication or encryption; any node can transmit any identifier. Mitigate with segmentation, gateways and AUTOSAR SecOC
protocols.description: Multi-master arbitrated differential bus with CRC and error confinement (error-passive, bus-off).

protocols.name: CAN FD
protocols.typical_rate: arbitration up to 1 Mbit/s, data phase 2-8 Mbit/s, 64-byte payload
protocols.security: No authentication or encryption; any node can transmit any identifier. Mitigate with segmentation, gateways and AUTOSAR SecOC
protocols.description: CAN with flexible data rate and larger payloads; requires FD-capable transceivers and careful topology.

protocols.name: CAN XL
protocols.typical_rate: data phase up to 20 Mbit/s, payload up to 2048 bytes
protocols.security: No authentication by default; CANsec (CiA 613-2) defines optional link-layer security
protocols.description: Third-generation CAN carrying larger frames (including Ethernet tunneling) at higher data rates.

protocols.name: CANopen
protocols.security: No authentication or encryption; any node can transmit any identifier. Mitigate with segmentation, gateways and AUTOSAR SecOC
protocols.description: CAN application layer with object dictionary, PDO/SDO, NMT and device profiles (CiA 402 drives).

protocols.name: SAE J1939
protocols.security: No authentication or encryption; any node can transmit any identifier. Mitigate with segmentation, gateways and AUTOSAR SecOC
protocols.description: Heavy-vehicle CAN higher layer using 29-bit IDs and PGNs; used in agricultural and off-highway robots.

protocols.name: DroneCAN
protocols.security: No authentication or encryption; any node can transmit any identifier. Mitigate with segmentation, gateways and AUTOSAR SecOC
protocols.description: Open UAV CAN protocol (UAVCAN v0 lineage) used by ArduPilot/PX4 peripherals: GNSS, ESCs, airspeed sensors.

protocols.name: OpenCyphal
protocols.typical_rate: CAN FD up to 5 Mbit/s data phase; also UDP/serial
protocols.security: No authentication or encryption; any node can transmit any identifier. Mitigate with segmentation, gateways and AUTOSAR SecOC
protocols.description: Lightweight publish/subscribe and RPC protocol (UAVCAN v1) over CAN, CAN FD, UDP or serial with DSDL types.

protocols.name: NMEA 2000
protocols.security: No authentication or encryption; any node can transmit any identifier. Mitigate with segmentation, gateways and AUTOSAR SecOC
protocols.description: Marine CAN network (J1939-based) for GNSS, sonar, autopilot and engine data on boats and USVs.

protocols.name: EtherCAT
protocols.typical_rate: 100 Mbit/s, cycle times down to ~100 us
protocols.topology: line/ring/tree, master-slave, processing on the fly
protocols.security: No built-in authentication or encryption; rely on network segmentation per IEC 62443
protocols.description: Ethernet-based fieldbus where frames are processed on the fly by slave controllers; distributed clocks for sub-us sync.

protocols.name: PROFINET
protocols.typical_rate: 100 Mbit/s; RT ~1 ms, IRT down to 31.25 us
protocols.security: Legacy installations unauthenticated; PI security classes add integrity/authentication; segment per IEC 62443
protocols.description: Industrial Ethernet protocol by PROFIBUS & PROFINET International with RT and IRT classes.

protocols.name: EtherNet/IP
protocols.security: Optional CIP Security (TLS/DTLS, device identity); most devices unauthenticated
protocols.description: ODVA Common Industrial Protocol (CIP) over standard TCP/UDP Ethernet.

protocols.name: Modbus RTU
protocols.security: None: no authentication, integrity only via CRC
protocols.description: Simple register-based master/slave protocol over RS-485/RS-232; ubiquitous in drives, meters and BMS.

protocols.name: Modbus TCP
protocols.security: None in classic Modbus TCP; Modbus/TCP Security (TLS, port 802) is optional and rarely deployed
protocols.description: Modbus application protocol over TCP/IP.

protocols.name: IO-Link
protocols.topology: point-to-point master port to device, 3-wire unshielded up to 20 m
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring
protocols.description: Point-to-point digital link to smart sensors/actuators with process data, parameters and diagnostics (IODD).

protocols.name: PROFIBUS DP/PA
protocols.security: No built-in authentication or encryption; rely on network segmentation per IEC 62443
protocols.description: Legacy serial fieldbus for factory (DP) and process (PA, intrinsically safe) automation.

protocols.name: DeviceNet
protocols.security: No authentication or encryption; any node can transmit any identifier. Mitigate with segmentation, gateways and AUTOSAR SecOC
protocols.description: CIP over CAN for device-level networking of sensors and drives (ODVA).

protocols.name: SERCOS III
protocols.security: No built-in authentication or encryption; rely on network segmentation per IEC 62443
protocols.description: Real-time Ethernet for motion control with synchronized drives; supports CIP Safety on Sercos.

protocols.name: Ethernet POWERLINK
protocols.topology: star/line/tree via hubs, managing node polls controlled nodes
protocols.security: No built-in authentication or encryption; rely on network segmentation per IEC 62443
protocols.description: Open real-time Ethernet (EPSG) using time-slot polling and CANopen device profiles.

protocols.name: CC-Link IE (Field/TSN)
protocols.security: No built-in authentication or encryption; rely on network segmentation per IEC 62443
protocols.description: CLPA gigabit industrial Ethernet; CC-Link IE TSN uses IEEE 802.1 TSN scheduling.

protocols.name: HART
protocols.security: None on wired HART
protocols.description: Digital FSK communication overlaid on 4-20 mA loops for configuration and diagnostics of process instruments.

protocols.name: Safety over EtherCAT (FSoE)
protocols.security: Black-channel safety layer: CRC, sequence counters and watchdogs protect against communication errors, not against deliberate attack
protocols.description: Functional-safety protocol carried in EtherCAT process data, up to SIL 3 / PL e.

protocols.name: PROFIsafe
protocols.topology: black channel over PROFINET or PROFIBUS
protocols.security: Black-channel safety layer: CRC, sequence counters and watchdogs protect against communication errors, not against deliberate attack
protocols.description: Functional-safety profile for PROFINET/PROFIBUS up to SIL 3; widely used for safe torque off and safe I/O.

protocols.name: CIP Safety
protocols.security: Black-channel safety layer: CRC, sequence counters and watchdogs protect against communication errors, not against deliberate attack
protocols.description: ODVA safety extension of CIP for safe I/O and drive functions up to SIL 3.

protocols.name: openSAFETY
protocols.security: Black-channel safety layer: CRC, sequence counters and watchdogs protect against communication errors, not against deliberate attack
protocols.description: Bus-independent safety protocol (originating with POWERLINK) up to SIL 3.

protocols.name: AS-Interface (AS-i)
protocols.topology: unshielded two-wire tree carrying data and power
protocols.security: None; relies on physical access control to the wiring
protocols.description: Simple sensor/actuator bus on a yellow flat cable; ASIsafe/Safety at Work variant for e-stops and light curtains.

protocols.name: Ethernet
protocols.security: No built-in authentication; IEEE 802.1X port access control and 802.1AE MACsec available
protocols.description: Standard wired LAN used for sensors (lidar, cameras), compute interconnect and higher protocols.

protocols.name: Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN)
protocols.security: Inherits Ethernet; MACsec and 802.1Qci per-stream filtering limit misbehaving talkers
protocols.description: IEEE 802.1 extensions for time sync, scheduled traffic and redundancy giving deterministic Ethernet.

protocols.name: Power over Ethernet
protocols.security: Not a data protocol; uncontrolled PSEs can power arbitrary devices
protocols.description: DC power over twisted-pair Ethernet cabling for cameras, APs and sensors.

protocols.name: Single Pair Ethernet 10BASE-T1L
protocols.security: As Ethernet; Ethernet-APL adds intrinsic-safety power, not security
protocols.description: Long-reach single-pair Ethernet physical layer; basis of Ethernet-APL for process field devices.

protocols.name: Wi-Fi
protocols.typical_rate: tens of Mbit/s to multiple Gbit/s (802.11n/ac/ax/be)
protocols.security: WPA3-SAE or WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise (802.1X/EAP); WPA2-PSK open to offline guessing; open networks unencrypted
protocols.description: WLAN on 2.4/5/6 GHz for robot-fleet links, teleoperation and IoT.

protocols.name: Wi-Fi HaLow
protocols.security: WPA3 (SAE/OWE) required for Wi-Fi CERTIFIED HaLow
protocols.description: Sub-1 GHz Wi-Fi for long-range low-power IoT (km range).

protocols.name: LTE (4G)
protocols.security: SIM-based mutual authentication (EPS-AKA) and air-interface ciphering; no user-plane integrity; private APN/VPN recommended
protocols.description: 4G cellular for remote telemetry and teleoperation of field robots.

protocols.name: 5G NR
protocols.topology: cellular star; public or private (non-public) networks
protocols.security: 5G-AKA/EAP-AKA', SUCI identity concealment, optional user-plane integrity
protocols.description: 5G New Radio for high-throughput, low-latency and private campus networks.

protocols.name: NB-IoT
protocols.security: 3GPP SIM-based authentication and ciphering
protocols.description: Narrowband LPWA cellular for low-rate static IoT sensors with deep coverage and PSM/eDRX sleep.

protocols.name: LTE-M (Cat M1)
protocols.security: 3GPP SIM-based authentication and ciphering
protocols.description: LPWA cellular with mobility and voice support for trackers and mobile IoT.

protocols.name: Bluetooth Low Energy
protocols.security: LE Secure Connections (ECDH P-256) with AES-CCM; Just Works pairing lacks MITM protection; legacy pairing weak
protocols.description: Low-power 2.4 GHz radio for wearables, beacons, provisioning and sensor links.

protocols.name: Bluetooth Classic (BR/EDR)
protocols.security: Secure Simple Pairing (Secure Connections mode recommended); legacy PIN pairing weak
protocols.description: Bluetooth BR/EDR for gamepads, audio and serial (SPP) links.

protocols.name: IEEE 802.15.4
protocols.security: Optional AES-CCM* link-layer security; key management left to upper layers
protocols.description: Low-rate WPAN PHY/MAC beneath Zigbee, Thread, WirelessHART and ISA100.11a.

protocols.name: Zigbee
protocols.topology: mesh with coordinator, routers and end devices
protocols.security: AES-128 CCM* network key; Zigbee 3.0 install codes; trust center controls joining; default link key widely known
protocols.description: Mesh networking for home/building IoT sensors, lights and switches.

protocols.name: Thread
protocols.security: AES-CCM link security with network key; commissioning via DTLS (EC-JPAKE)
protocols.description: Low-power IPv6 mesh, the main low-power transport for Matter.

protocols.name: Z-Wave
protocols.security: S2 security (ECDH Curve25519 key exchange, AES-128); legacy S0 weak; unsecured inclusion possible
protocols.description: Sub-GHz home automation mesh for locks, sensors and switches.

protocols.name: LoRaWAN
protocols.security: AES-128 session keys (NwkSKey/AppSKey; split network keys in 1.1); OTAA preferred over ABP; gateways forward without decrypting
protocols.description: LPWAN MAC over LoRa modulation for long-range, low-rate battery sensors.

protocols.name: LoRa (raw PHY)
protocols.security: None at the PHY; application must add encryption and authentication
protocols.description: Semtech chirp spread spectrum modulation used directly (without LoRaWAN) for custom long-range links and Meshtastic-style meshes.

protocols.name: mioty
protocols.typical_rate: ~400 bit/s per telegram, very high node density
protocols.security: AES-128 encryption and authentication of telegrams
protocols.description: LPWAN using telegram splitting for interference robustness in industrial IoT.

protocols.name: DECT NR+
protocols.typical_rate: up to several Mbit/s; low latency mode
protocols.security: Link-layer ciphering and integrity defined in the standard
protocols.description: Non-cellular IMT-2020 radio in the 1.9 GHz band for license-exempt industrial mesh IoT.

protocols.name: WirelessHART
protocols.topology: TDMA mesh with network manager and gateway
protocols.security: Mandatory AES-128 CCM, join keys and per-session keys managed by security manager
protocols.description: Wireless extension of HART for process instruments.

protocols.name: ISA100.11a
protocols.security: AES-128 CCM link and transport security with security manager
protocols.description: Industrial wireless sensor networking standard for process automation.

protocols.name: ESP-NOW
protocols.security: Optional CCMP encryption with PMK/LMK for a limited number of peers; unencrypted by default
protocols.description: Espressif connectionless 2.4 GHz protocol over Wi-Fi vendor action frames for low-latency ESP32 links.

protocols.name: Ultra-wideband (UWB)
protocols.security: 802.15.4z Scrambled Timestamp Sequence (STS) protects ranging against distance spoofing
protocols.description: Impulse-radio UWB for precise indoor positioning and secure ranging.

protocols.name: Satellite link
protocols.topology: star via satellite and ground station
protocols.security: Provider-dependent; treat as untrusted transport and use end-to-end TLS/VPN
protocols.description: LEO/GEO satellite connectivity for remote field, marine and agricultural robots.

protocols.name: Futaba S.BUS
protocols.typical_rate: 100 kbit/s inverted UART, 7-14 ms frames, 16 channels
protocols.security: None (wired leg); RF link security depends on the RC system
protocols.description: Serial RC receiver output carrying 16 proportional channels plus failsafe flags.

protocols.name: Crossfire / CRSF
protocols.typical_rate: 416.666 kbit/s UART; up to 1000 Hz packets (ExpressLRS)
protocols.topology: point-to-point receiver to flight controller, bidirectional telemetry
protocols.security: None on the serial link; ExpressLRS binding phrase is not cryptographic authentication
protocols.description: TBS Crossfire serial protocol (also used by ExpressLRS) carrying RC channels and telemetry.

protocols.name: RC PPM (CPPM)
protocols.security: None
protocols.description: Pulse-position modulated sum signal of RC channels on a single wire; legacy.

protocols.name: DSRC / V2X
protocols.security: IEEE 1609.2 certificate-signed messages with SCMS/PKI; no confidentiality for broadcast safety messages
protocols.description: Vehicle-to-everything messaging (BSM, SPaT/MAP) for road robots and infrastructure; C-V2X (3GPP PC5) is the cellular alternative.

protocols.name: Precision Time Protocol
protocols.security: Unauthenticated in common profiles; IEEE 1588-2019 optional authentication TLV
protocols.description: Network clock synchronization for sensor fusion timestamps, TSN and motion control.

protocols.name: TLS
protocols.security: TLS 1.3 provides authenticated encryption; use certificate validation and mutual TLS for devices
protocols.description: Transport Layer Security protecting MQTT, HTTP, gRPC, OPC UA (HTTPS) and other TCP protocols; DTLS (RFC 9147) for UDP.

protocols.name: MQTT
protocols.typical_rate: msg rates from 1/h to thousands/s per broker client
protocols.security: No security in the protocol itself; rely on TLS, client authentication (username/password, X.509) and broker topic ACLs
protocols.description: Lightweight broker-based pub/sub over TCP for telemetry and fleet messaging.

protocols.name: CoAP
protocols.security: DTLS (RFC 9147) or OSCORE (RFC 8613) object security
protocols.description: RESTful protocol for constrained devices over UDP.

protocols.name: OMA LwM2M
protocols.security: DTLS/TLS with PSK, raw public key or X.509; OSCORE supported from 1.1
protocols.description: Device-management and telemetry protocol on CoAP with the IPSO/LwM2M object model (firmware update, connectivity, sensors).

protocols.name: OPC UA
protocols.security: Built-in security: SecurityMode None/Sign/SignAndEncrypt with X.509 application certificates and user tokens; 'None' must not be used in production
protocols.description: Platform-independent industrial information modeling and communication (companion specs incl. OPC UA Robotics).

protocols.name: OPC UA PubSub
protocols.security: Message signing/encryption with group keys distributed by a Security Key Service (SKS)
protocols.description: Publish-subscribe extension of OPC UA for cyclic data, including over TSN (OPC UA FX).

protocols.name: HTTP/REST
protocols.security: TLS (HTTPS) plus application authentication (OAuth 2.0, API keys, mTLS)
protocols.description: Resource-oriented HTTP APIs for configuration, fleet and cloud integration.

protocols.name: WebSocket
protocols.typical_rate: full-duplex over a single TCP connection
protocols.security: Use wss:// (TLS); validate Origin; authentication left to the application
protocols.description: Bidirectional streaming over HTTP upgrade for dashboards, rosbridge and teleoperation UIs.

protocols.name: gRPC
protocols.security: TLS/mTLS channel credentials plus per-call tokens
protocols.description: High-performance RPC framework (CNCF) using Protocol Buffers over HTTP/2.

protocols.name: Matter
protocols.security: PASE (SPAKE2+) commissioning, CASE (SIGMA) operational sessions, Device Attestation Certificates, ACLs per fabric
protocols.description: IP-based smart-home application standard with a common data model of clusters and device types.

protocols.name: BACnet
protocols.security: Legacy BACnet/IP and MS/TP unauthenticated; BACnet Secure Connect (BACnet/SC) adds TLS over WebSockets
protocols.description: Building automation protocol for HVAC, lighting, access and elevators.

protocols.name: KNX
protocols.security: Legacy unauthenticated; KNX Data Secure and KNX IP Secure use AES-128 CCM
protocols.description: Home and building control standard for lighting, blinds and HVAC.

protocols.name: NMEA 0183
protocols.security: None
protocols.description: ASCII sentence protocol output by GNSS receivers, compasses and marine instruments.

protocols.name: SOME/IP
protocols.security: None natively; use SecOC, TLS or IPsec
protocols.description: Scalable service-oriented middleware over IP used in automotive ECUs.

protocols.name: ONVIF
protocols.security: WS-UsernameToken/HTTP digest, optional TLS; default credentials are a common weakness
protocols.description: Interoperability standard for IP cameras: discovery, PTZ, streaming and events.

protocols.name: RTSP
protocols.typical_rate: control channel for RTP media streams
protocols.security: Basic/digest authentication; RTSPS and SRTP optional; often deployed in cleartext
protocols.description: Stream control protocol for IP camera video (RTP payloads).

protocols.name: WebRTC
protocols.security: Mandatory DTLS-SRTP media encryption; signaling security is application-defined
protocols.description: Low-latency real-time audio/video/data for teleoperation and remote monitoring.

protocols.name: DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0
protocols.typical_rate: 57.6 kbit/s-4.5 Mbit/s over TTL or RS-485
protocols.security: None
protocols.description: ROBOTIS packet protocol for smart servos: control table reads/writes, sync/bulk read-write, CRC-16.

protocols.name: MAVLink
protocols.security: MAVLink 2 optional message signing (SHA-256 based, 48-bit signature) for authentication; no encryption; v1 unauthenticated
protocols.description: Lightweight messaging for drones and ground control (PX4, ArduPilot), carried over telemetry radios or IP.

protocols.name: SNMP
protocols.security: v1/v2c use plaintext community strings; v3 USM provides authentication and privacy
protocols.description: Network management of switches, UPSs and gateways.

protocols.name: AMQP 1.0
protocols.typical_rate: broker or peer messaging over TCP
protocols.security: SASL authentication plus TLS
protocols.description: Reliable enterprise messaging protocol used by cloud IoT hubs and message brokers.

protocols.name: Eclipse Sparkplug B
protocols.security: Relies on MQTT TLS and broker ACLs; no payload authentication
protocols.description: MQTT topic namespace, state management and payload definition for industrial IoT.

protocols.name: DNP3
protocols.security: Secure Authentication v5 (HMAC challenge-response) optional; TLS per IEC 62351; legacy unauthenticated
protocols.description: SCADA protocol for utilities (energy, water) used by substation and grid-inspection integrations.

protocols.name: NTRIP
protocols.typical_rate: RTCM corrections ~1 Hz, a few kbit/s
protocols.security: NTRIP v1 basic auth in cleartext; v2 supports TLS
protocols.description: Networked transport of RTCM GNSS corrections from casters to RTK rovers.

protocols.name: W3C WoT Thing Description
protocols.topology: description of a Thing's interaction affordances
protocols.security: Declares securityDefinitions (basic, digest, bearer, OAuth2, PSK); does not itself enforce security
protocols.description: JSON-LD description of properties, actions and events of IoT devices with protocol bindings.

protocols.name: Asset Administration Shell (AAS)
protocols.security: API security per implementation (TLS, OAuth 2.0); AAS security metamodel defines access rules
protocols.description: Industry 4.0 standardized digital twin with submodels (nameplate, technical data) and HTTP API.

protocols.name: ROS 1
protocols.security: None: XML-RPC master and topics are unauthenticated; ROS 1 is end-of-life (Noetic EOL May 2025)
protocols.description: Robot Operating System 1 with roscore name service; legacy systems.

protocols.name: ROS 2
protocols.security: Off by default; SROS2 enables DDS Security (authentication, access control, encryption)
protocols.description: Robot Operating System 2 built on pluggable RMW middleware.

protocols.name: SROS2 (ROS 2 security)
protocols.security: X.509 identity and permissions certificates applied through DDS Security plugins
protocols.description: ROS 2 tooling that generates keystores, enclaves and governance/permissions for DDS Security.

protocols.name: OMG DDS (RTPS)
protocols.security: DDS Security plugins (authentication, access control, cryptography) optional; unsecured by default
protocols.description: Data Distribution Service with QoS policies; default ROS 2 transport.

protocols.name: Eclipse Zenoh
protocols.security: TLS/QUIC with mTLS, user/password authentication and access control rules; off by default
protocols.description: Pub/sub/query protocol spanning microcontrollers to cloud; rmw_zenoh RMW for ROS 2.

protocols.name: micro-ROS
protocols.security: XRCE-DDS link has no built-in security; secure the transport and agent side
protocols.description: ROS 2 client library for microcontrollers communicating through a micro-ROS agent.

protocols.name: Eclipse iceoryx
protocols.security: Relies on OS user/group permissions on shared memory
protocols.description: Zero-copy inter-process communication used as shared-memory transport (e.g. Cyclone DDS).

protocols.name: dora-rs
protocols.security: No built-in authentication; local process trust
protocols.description: Dataflow-oriented robotics middleware using zero-copy Arrow messages, aimed at AI pipelines.

protocols.name: VDA 5050
protocols.typical_rate: JSON over MQTT, state messages ~1 Hz or on change
protocols.topology: master control - vehicle via MQTT broker
protocols.security: Relies on MQTT TLS, client authentication and broker ACLs
protocols.description: Interface between AGV/AMR fleets and master control: orders, actions, state and visualization.

protocols.name: MassRobotics Interoperability Standard
protocols.topology: robots report to a shared server
protocols.security: Use wss:// (TLS) and server authentication
protocols.description: Status and identity reporting of heterogeneous AMRs to a common server for shared-space coordination.

protocols.name: Open-RMF
protocols.topology: central traffic/task managers with fleet adapters
protocols.security: Inherits ROS 2 security (SROS2); API server should use TLS and authentication
protocols.description: Open Robotics Middleware Framework for multi-fleet traffic, task allocation and infrastructure (doors, lifts) integration.
